blockers.summary: The upload to jammy-proposed was rejected from the queue as 'languishing for over a month', so the fix is not in -proposed and must be re-uploaded.

The change alters rados_connect_timeout semantics: 0 now means no timeout (before, <=0 meant use the default), and <0 means use the Ceph config. Deployments such as charm-glance that set 0 could now wait forever. The SRU's 'Where problems could occur' section does not cover this regression risk.
The reviewer asked for the [Impact] section to be rewritten to explain clearly what is fixed and why. There is no sign it was updated; the description still reads unclearly.

The only verification is PPA autopkgtests plus a vague mention of an earlier test package. There is no documented functional verification of the timeout behaviour, and the test plan implies a timeout value of 300 where the semantic change makes 0 and negative values the risky cases.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

Are they just lacking reviews in the mailing list? Or are there other concerns?

I understand we also need an apparmor patch for libvirt, and a versioned breaks in qemu to force the upgrade of libvirt if it's installed, right?
